correctness.rationale: Affinely y^p-y=x^m is integral because m prime to p gives Artin-Schreier class of non-p-divisible pole, and smooth since F_y=-1. At infinity cusp z^(m-p)(1-z^(p-1))=x^m has one branch with valuations ord(x)=m-p, ord(z)=m. Generic projective polar derivative F_Z has minimum order m(m-p-1), including smooth a=1 case order 0, leaving m(m-1)-m(m-p-1)=pm of affine polar intersections. Affine dual coordinates u=m x^(m-1), v=y+m x^m; if p does not divide m-1 then dv/du=x recovering x,y and separable birational Gauss. If m=kp+1, u=(x^k)^p,v=y^p, and (x^k,y) generate the same function field since x=(y^p-y)/(x^k)^p; Gauss degree pure inseparable p. Independently eliminated x symbolically over F_p for (2,5),(3,5),(3,7); total resultant degrees 10,15,21 respectively, with expected p-th multiplicities and reduced dual degrees 5,15,7. Finite resultants supplement valuation proof.
residual_risks: Theorem is about geometric reduced dual degree, not scheme-theoretic dual, more general Artin-Schreier polynomials or p|m.
